assumptions: piSignage may be installed on the same Raspberry Pi OS host, but neither CVE description states this.
Raspberry Pi OS default or discovered credentials may map to piSignage web credentials, but neither CVE description states credential reuse.
Administrator OS access may allow discovery or creation of piSignage credentials, but no supplied description establishes such a method.
The source CVE's default-password condition may be true on the target, but the environment observations are absent.

evidence_quotes.quote: Raspberry Pi OS through 5.10 has the raspberry default password for the pi account. If not changed, attackers can gain administrator privileges.
allows a remote attacker (authenticated as a low-privilege user) to download arbitrary files from the Raspberry Pi via api/settings/log?file=../ path traversal

missing_conditions: verified unchanged default password on the target Raspberry Pi OS host
verified same-host deployment or explicit network/service relationship between the Raspberry Pi OS host and the piSignage web application
verified credential linkage or reuse between Raspberry Pi OS credentials and a piSignage low-privilege web user
attacker possession or acquisition of authenticated low-privilege piSignage credentials
verified piSignage version < 2.6.4 on the target
network reachability to the piSignage web application/API
explicit evidence that Raspberry Pi OS administrator access can obtain the required piSignage low-privilege web session
response.reason: CVE-2021-38759 describes a conditional OS-level effect: Raspberry Pi OS through 5.10 has a default password for the pi account, and if it is not changed, attackers can gain administrator privileges. CVE-2019-20354 requires an authenticated low-privilege piSignage user and piSignage before 2.6.4 to exploit the path traversal and download arbitrary files. The edge asserts that default system credentials or discovered credentials yield an authenticated low-privilege piSignage web session. The supplied descriptions do not establish piSignage deployment on the same host, credential reuse, or a method to obtain piSignage credentials from OS administrator access. The bridge is therefore conditional and potentially plausible only under unverified assumptions; as currently evidenced, it cannot enter a strict supported graph.
